guides.title: Render escaped HTML on the server
guides.summary: Use the server entrypoint to turn an HTML template into a string.
guides.markdown:
Import html and renderToString from the public server entrypoint. Interpolate text values into html templates. The renderer escapes text rather than interpreting it as markup.

Do not concatenate untrusted text into HTML source or use unsafe raw-HTML helpers for it. Escaping text does not authorize a request or validate application URLs. Server rendering produces an HTML string. It does not attach browser event handlers or hydrate an application.

guides.title: Select template branches and optional attributes
guides.summary: Render conditional content without building HTML strings.
guides.markdown: Use `when` to select a branch and `choose` to match a value with strict equality. Their callbacks run while the template expression is evaluated. Use `nothing` for an empty child value. `ifDefined(undefined)` omits an attribute; other values, including `null`, `false`, and `0`, are serialized as values. HTML escaping does not validate URL schemes or authorize a destination.

guides.title: Render lists with stable item keys
guides.summary: Use keyed repeat for lists whose DOM items should keep their identity.
guides.markdown: `repeat(items, keyFn, templateFn)` gives the browser renderer a stable key for each item so it can retain matching DOM nodes when the list changes. Server rendering emits the initial ordered markup; it does not prove browser node reuse. Use `join` when you need a renderable separator between values. Plain arrays and `map` are enough when item identity does not matter.

guides.title: Render current form values before hydration
guides.summary: Seed input, checkbox, and textarea values in server-rendered HTML.
guides.markdown: Use `.value=${bind(state, path)}` and `.checked=${bind(state, path)}` to render the current field values. `live(value)` supplies the current value when the renderer reconciles an existing DOM property. On the server these helpers only produce initial markup; client rendering or hydration is required for browser write-back. A binding does not validate submitted data or authorize a server action.

guides.title: Compose component CSS from reviewed values
guides.summary: Use css tagged templates for static styles and reserve unsafeCSS for trusted values.
guides.markdown: `css` accepts numeric interpolations and other `CSSResult` values. It rejects ordinary strings, so use static styles and typed numbers for normal composition. `unsafeCSS` marks a string as trusted CSS; it does not sanitize it. Never pass user input, request data, or other untrusted values to `unsafeCSS`.
